\section[accusare]{accusare — to accuse}

\label{lesson:IT-C391-accusare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for unlawful, then the Italian for unauthorised.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: accusare}
\textbf{accusare} — \textquotedblleft{}to accuse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Mi accusano di aver preso i soldi, ma non è vero.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{They accuse me of taking the money, but it is not true.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Accusare qualcuno di qualcosa}. \emph{Accusare un dolore} — to feel a pain.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{accusare} is inherited from Latin \emph{accūsāre} \textquotedblleft{}to call to account, to accuse\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built from \emph{ad} \textquotedblleft{}to\textquotedblright{} and \emph{causa} \textquotedblleft{}a case, a lawsuit\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{accusare}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{accusare}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{accusare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for unlawful, then the Italian for unauthorised, then say \emph{accusare} again
\end{itemize}

What does accusare mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To accuse\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[l'accusa]{l'accusa — the accusation, the charge; the prosecution}

\label{lesson:IT-C391-accusa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for unauthorised, then the Italian for to accuse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'accusa}
\textbf{l'accusa} — \textquotedblleft{}the accusation, the charge; the prosecution\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
L'accusa è falsa: quella sera ero a casa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The accusation is false: that evening I was at home.}
\end{quote}

In court, \emph{l'accusa} is the prosecution.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{accusa} is built on \emph{accusare} \textquotedblleft{}to accuse\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Latin \emph{accūsāre} (EtymDB), on \emph{causa} \textquotedblleft{}a case, a lawsuit\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for unauthorised, then the Italian for to accuse, then say \emph{l'accusa} again

\section[il ladro]{il ladro — the thief}

\label{lesson:IT-C391-ladro}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to accuse, then the Italian for the accusation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il ladro}
\textbf{il ladro} — \textquotedblleft{}the thief\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il ladro è entrato dalla finestra.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The thief came in through the window.}
\end{quote}

A woman is \emph{la ladra}. \emph{Al ladro!} — stop thief!

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ladro} is inherited from Latin \emph{latrō, latrōnis} \textquotedblleft{}a hired soldier; a robber, a bandit\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la querela]{la querela — the criminal complaint, the lawsuit}

\label{lesson:IT-C391-querela}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the accusation, then the Italian for the thief.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la querela}
\textbf{la querela} — \textquotedblleft{}the criminal complaint, the lawsuit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se continua a insultarmi, sporgo querela.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{If he keeps insulting me, I will take legal action.}
\end{quote}

Legal Italian: \emph{sporgere querela} — to lodge a complaint. Stress: \emph{querèla}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{querela} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{querēla} \textquotedblleft{}a complaint, a lament\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{querī} \textquotedblleft{}to complain\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la corruzione]{la corruzione — the corruption}

\label{lesson:IT-C391-corruzione}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the thief, then the Italian for the criminal complaint.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la corruzione}
\textbf{la corruzione} — \textquotedblleft{}the corruption\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il sindaco è accusato di corruzione.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The mayor is accused of corruption.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Corrotto} — corrupt.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{corruzione} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{corruptiō, corruptiōnis} \textquotedblleft{}a spoiling, a bribing\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{corrumpere} \textquotedblleft{}to break up, to spoil\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{rumpere} \textquotedblleft{}to break\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
